commonIssues.symptom: Original Simplicity board failure (Sunline 2000 / Predator / 3-6 t Sunline package units): blower will not run even with the thermostat fan switched ON, so heat locks out on the high limit (no-heat call); or unit dead / erratic with the LED steady on or no heartbeat
likelyCauses: Failed original Simplicity control board (HVAC-Talk 'York Sunline unit circuit board failure': repeated board failures on York 3-6 t Sunline package units across multiple jobs, presenting as the blower not starting and heat locking out on limit)
Blower contactor coil failing / drawing the board output down (a factory rep in the same thread advised replacing the blower contactor together with the board)
Blown board fuse from a shorted 24 V field wire
Transformer failure
checks: Verify 24 VAC at R-C and the board fuse
With G called, check for 24 V at the board's blower output and at the blower contactor coil; ohm the contactor coil - replace the blower contactor with the board if it is suspect
Check for a shorted thermostat cable or economizer wiring before replacing the board

If the LED is steady on, or the blower output never energizes with good supply, replace the UCB (replacement kits reported in the thread: S1-33109150001 / S1-33109150002, S1-33103005000 - verify the kit for the unit with the distributor)
sources: HVAC-Talk thread 'York Sunline unit circuit board failure' (1273311)

commonIssues.symptom: Compressors cycle 10 min on / 5 min off, or stay off while the economizer free-cools, in cool weather; flash code 10 on the board
likelyCauses: Low ambient switch closed (normal: normally open, closes ~45 F, opens ~55 F) - flash code 10 is a notice, not a lockout (York Central Tech Talk)
Economizer software switch set wrong for the installed equipment (ON = compressors held off during free cooling; OFF = 10 on / 5 off cycling)
Failed low ambient switch
checks: Note outdoor ambient; above 55 F the switch should be open
Ohm the LAS and its wiring to the UCB
Confirm the economizer switch setting on the board matches whether an economizer is installed
sources: York Central Tech Talk 'Simplicity Diagnostics Flash Codes' (2013)
JustAnswer York rooftop flash code 10 thread

commonIssues.symptom: Gas heat lockout / no ignition on rooftop
likelyCauses: Combustion-air pressure switch not proving (blocked flue, failed inducer/combustion motor, cracked hose)
Dirty flame sensor
Rollout switch tripped (manual reset) from heat-exchanger or burner problems
Gas valve or supply pressure problem
checks: Read the IGC flash code (separate table from the UCB)
Check inlet/manifold gas pressure
Verify pressure switch closes when the combustion motor runs; inspect flue and hoses
Clean the flame sensor and check the microamp signal
Inspect the heat exchanger if rollout has tripped

commonIssues.symptom: Low pressure / freeze lockouts on Z-series or SE-controlled units
likelyCauses: Dirty filters or slipping/broken blower belt (low airflow)
Low charge / leak
Economizer damper stuck open in cold weather
checks: Filters, belt tension, blower wheel
Suction pressure and superheat
Economizer minimum position and actuator operation

commonIssues.symptom: Smart Equipment unit runs but not to setpoint; sensor alarms on SE-SPU
likelyCauses: Failed or unplugged SAT/RAT/OAT sensors
Controller configured for the wrong mode (thermostat vs. sensor/BAS control)
Economizer or occupancy settings not commissioned
checks: Read the SE-SPU Alarms menu
Ohm sensors against the resistance table
Review the controller Setup / Details menus (control mode, setpoints, economizer enable)

commonIssues.symptom: Economizer not modulating / free cooling never used
likelyCauses: Failed actuator or economizer logic module
Bad outdoor enthalpy/dry-bulb sensor or changeover setpoint
Linkage disconnected
checks: Command minimum position and observe damper travel
Check 24 V and control signal at the actuator
Check the OA sensor and changeover setting

notes: Coverage summary: serial rules are the strongest part of this pack (three formats, many agreeing decoders). Model formats decode category, series letter, tonnage and (Z/D-series) the heat-type letter and heat code; voltage, options and revision positions were NOT transcribed from a nomenclature page and are left undecoded rather than guessed. Sun Core ZX/ZY/ZQ/ZL (2020+) is recognised but its 04-14 size codes are not converted to tons.

Control platforms are partial: simplicity-ucb carries the UCB flash table (steady/heartbeat/off, 1-14) and ICB table (1-10) from IOM search summaries; smart-equipment carries the critical alarms, selected service/FDD alarms; intelli-comfort (15-25 t D-series, single secondary source) and millennium-simplicity-elite (codes 1-8 of 43) are separate platforms. JCI IQ boards and Sun Premier 25-80 t fault tables are not included.
Electrical and common-issue sections are generic field practice from memory and are marked low/inferred; treat the unit's wiring-diagram legend as authoritative.
Web-search budget was exhausted during authoring; a second pass with the JCI documentation portal should raise the model-format and control-platform coverage.

Residential York/Coleman/Luxaire nomenclature (YHJF/YCJF splits, P*HU/P*UR furnaces, AHX air handlers, e.g. YHJF18S41S1A, AHX24B3XH21A, P4HUB16N06401A, H2DB024S06B) is not decoded by this pack; only the serial date applies to those plates.

2026-10-20 additions: chiller panels (YVAA/YVFA IPU2/IPU3 fault codes 1-62 + operational/warning codes from SI0630 and the Style B BAS list; YR OptiView BAS enumerations; YK OptiView safety/cycling message names from 160.75-EG1; full YMC2 Mod B (160.84-OM1) and YVAM (160.88-OM1) OptiView message tables), the residential TM9V*MP furnace control LED table (438335-UIM-B-0509) and the YK Style F nomenclature. Still missing: Hx3 / Affinity communicating alert codes, other residential furnace boards (TG9S/TM8 single-stage, YP9C/TM9M modulating, 2020+ boards), residential nomenclature, the YK 160.54-O1 message descriptions, YK Style H / YZ / YD message lists, YCAV/YCIV/YLAA/YCAL fault lists.
Coleman and Luxaire (and Guardian) residential furnaces share JCI Unitary Products controls; the TM9V table applies only where the board/label matches - always read the label on the blower door.
